sections.title: Intermediate Concept of Coding-Decoding
sections.content: At Level 2, Coding-Decoding questions involve more than one rule. A word may be shifted, rearranged, or converted into numbers in multiple steps. The key skill is to break the pattern into small logical steps and test them carefully.

sections.title: Double Operation Pattern
sections.content: Sometimes two operations are applied. First, change the alphabet position (like +2 or -3). Then reverse the word or rearrange it. Example: GAME → +1 gives HBNF, then reversing gives FNBH.

sections.title: Alternate Letter Rule
sections.content: Different rules may apply to alternate letters. For example, 1st, 3rd, 5th letters may be increased by +2, while 2nd, 4th letters may be decreased by -1.

sections.title: Alphabetical Difference Pattern
sections.content: Some codes follow a consistent gap between letters. Example: BDFH follows a +2 pattern. Identifying such differences helps solve the code faster.

sections.title: Number-Letter Combination Coding
sections.content: A word may be converted into a number using the sum of letter positions, and then combined with a letter. Example: CODE → C=3, O=15, D=4, E=5. Total = 27. Code may be written as 27E.

sections.title: Sentence-Based Logical Coding
sections.content: In sentence coding, multiple sentences are given. Identify common words and match them with repeated codes. Logical elimination is important at this level.

sections.title: Rearrangement Pattern
sections.content: Letters may be rearranged in a fixed order like 2-4-1-3. Recognizing this positional change is important for solving such questions.

sections.title: Important Strategies
sections.content: 1. Check simple shifts first. 2. Look for alternate patterns. 3. Break the process into steps. 4. Compare answer options logically. 5. Confirm the rule with at least two letters.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Assuming only one rule is used. 2. Ignoring alternate letter changes. 3. Calculation errors in alphabet positions. 4. Not verifying the pattern fully before selecting an answer.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 2 Coding-Decoding includes multiple operations, alternate letter rules, number-letter combinations, and rearrangement patterns. Careful step-by-step analysis improves accuracy.

tricks.title: 27 Opposite Rule
tricks.explanation: Opposite letters in the alphabet always add up to 27.

tricks.title: Alternate Position Check
tricks.explanation: Separate odd and even position letters and test different rules.

tricks.title: Step-by-Step Testing
tricks.explanation: Apply one operation at a time and check if it matches the coded word.

tricks.title: Difference Analysis Trick
tricks.explanation: Check if the difference between letters is constant.

tricks.title: Sum Plus Letter Trick
tricks.explanation: Add all letter positions and attach the last letter.

tricks.title: Common Word Lock Method
tricks.explanation: In sentence coding, fix the code of repeated words first.
tricks.example: If RAM appears twice with same code, that code belongs to RAM.

tricks.title: Option Elimination Strategy
tricks.explanation: Remove options that do not follow the identified pattern.

tricks.title: Half Alphabet Shift
tricks.explanation: Try shifting letters by +13 to test pattern.

tricks.title: Reverse Plus Shift Combo
tricks.explanation: First reverse the word, then apply shifting.
